title: Gratitude is not a bargain
hook: Notice a blessing without turning it into a demand for more.
body: Quran 14:7 connects gratitude with Allah's promise of increase. This is an explanatory paraphrase, not a literal translation. The verse invites thankfulness; it is not a formula for getting a particular possession on a deadline. As a personal reflection, name one blessing today and consider how to use it well. Gratitude can begin with what is already present.
takeaway: Name one blessing and one responsible way to use it.

sources.title: Quran 14:7 — Ibrahim

quiz.question: Which reflection fits this lesson?
options: Gratitude guarantees a specific purchase tomorrow
Receive blessings thankfully without setting Allah a deadline
Only large blessings deserve thanks
quiz.explanation: The verse encourages gratitude, not a transactional promise about a particular worldly result.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Gratitude is not a bargain. Name one blessing and one responsible way to use it.

title: You cannot finish the list
hook: A short gratitude list is a beginning, not an inventory of everything.
body: Quran 16:18 reminds people that Allah's blessings cannot be fully counted and describes Him as forgiving and merciful. This is an explanatory paraphrase. Try tracing one ordinary meal: water, soil, transport, preparation and the people involved. The exercise is a reflection, not a prescribed ritual. Its purpose is to notice how much support can sit behind something that feels routine.
takeaway: Trace one everyday blessing beyond its most obvious source.

sources.title: Quran 16:18 — An-Nahl

quiz.question: What does this verse remind us about blessings?
options: Only unusual events count
A complete list is required daily
They exceed our ability to count them fully
quiz.explanation: The verse emphasizes the abundance of Allah's blessings, not a required counting exercise.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: You cannot finish the list. Trace one everyday blessing beyond its most obvious source.

title: Remember, then give thanks
hook: An ordinary pause can become a moment of attention to Allah.
body: Quran 2:152 calls people to remember Allah and thank Him rather than be ungrateful. This is an explanatory paraphrase, not a quotation. For a personal practice, pause after noticing something helpful and turn your attention to Allah with thanks. The suggested pause is simply an application of the reminder; the verse does not prescribe this particular timing or a new ritual.
takeaway: Let one ordinary moment prompt sincere remembrance and thanks.

sources.title: Quran 2:152 — Al-Baqarah

quiz.question: Which pair appears in the verse's reminder?
options: Remembrance and gratitude
Competition and publicity
Wealth and popularity
quiz.explanation: The verse brings remembrance of Allah and thankfulness together.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Remember, then give thanks. Let one ordinary moment prompt sincere remembrance and thanks.

title: Speak of a blessing with humility
hook: You can acknowledge good without making yourself the centre.
body: Quran 93:11 directs the Prophet to speak of his Lord's blessing. This is an explanatory paraphrase. Read alongside the preceding reminders about the orphan and the person asking for help, it invites reflection on gratitude and care. A practical application is to acknowledge a blessing without belittling someone else's hardship. This lesson offers a reflection, not a ruling about what must be shared publicly.
takeaway: Acknowledge one blessing without comparing your life to someone else's.

sources.title: Quran 93:11 — Ad-Duhaa, with surrounding verses

quiz.question: Which example best matches this reflection?
options: Using success to mock another person
Thanking Allah while remaining considerate of others
Treating every blessing as personal superiority
quiz.explanation: Humble acknowledgement fits the reflection; boasting at another person's expense does not.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Speak of a blessing with humility. Acknowledge one blessing without comparing your life to someone else's.

title: Difference is an invitation to know
hook: A name, accent or nationality is not a measure of someone's worth.
body: Quran 49:13 addresses humanity, describes peoples and tribes as a means of knowing one another, and connects honour before Allah with righteousness. This is an explanatory paraphrase. A daily application is to meet someone with curiosity rather than a stereotype. Ask a respectful question and listen to the answer. You do not need to rank people by ancestry, appearance or social position.
takeaway: Replace one assumption about a person with a respectful question.

sources.title: Quran 49:13 — Al-Hujurat

quiz.question: What purpose for peoples and tribes is mentioned?
options: To know one another
To rank accents
To prove inherited superiority
quiz.explanation: The verse identifies knowing one another, not inherited status, as the purpose of these differences.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Difference is an invitation to know. Replace one assumption about a person with a respectful question.

title: Check the reason before the action
hook: The same visible action can begin with very different intentions.
body: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1, the Prophet teaches the importance of intentions and illustrates it through migration undertaken for different aims. This is an explanatory paraphrase. Before a helpful action, ask yourself what you are trying to serve. Wanting recognition can be a prompt to reconsider your motive. This reflection does not let us judge another person's heart from what we see outside.
takeaway: Before one good action, quietly clarify your intention.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1 — Intentions

quiz.question: What is the appropriate focus of this intention check?
options: Guessing everyone else's hidden motives
Making the action look impressive
Examining your own purpose
quiz.explanation: The practical check concerns your own intention, not claims about another person's inner state.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Check the reason before the action. Before one good action, quietly clarify your intention.

title: Not every reply needs to be sent
hook: A draft can stay a draft when it adds only harm.
body: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018 includes the teaching to speak good or remain silent, alongside care for neighbours and guests. This is an explanatory paraphrase. Before sending an irritated reply, ask whether it is truthful, useful and considerate. You can rewrite it, wait, or leave it unsent. This is not an instruction to stay silent about harm when someone needs help or protection.
takeaway: Reread one message for benefit before pressing send.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018 — Speech, neighbours and guests

quiz.question: What is a sensible application before an angry reply?
options: Send it immediately because it is honest
Check whether it brings good and revise if needed
Never report wrongdoing
quiz.explanation: The lesson encourages beneficial speech without turning silence into an excuse to ignore harm.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Not every reply needs to be sent. Reread one message for benefit before pressing send.

title: Neighbour care starts close to home
hook: Consider the people who share the space around your door.
body: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018 links faith with not harming one's neighbour and with honouring a guest. This is an explanatory paraphrase. A practical reflection is to notice the effect of your noise, rubbish or use of shared space. You might also offer appropriate help without intruding. These everyday examples apply the teaching; they are not a new checklist of religious obligations.
takeaway: Reduce one avoidable inconvenience for a neighbour today.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 6018 — Treatment of neighbours

quiz.question: Which action fits neighbour care?
options: Keeping shared access clear
Ignoring the effect of your noise
Offering help only for public praise
quiz.explanation: Keeping shared access clear is a concrete way to avoid inconveniencing neighbours.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Neighbour care starts close to home. Reduce one avoidable inconvenience for a neighbour today.

title: Make one burden lighter
hook: Helpful support does not always need to be dramatic.
body: Sahih Muslim 2699a describes the virtue of relieving another person's distress and helping someone in difficulty. This is an explanatory paraphrase. Ask what would actually help before offering a solution. Carrying a task, explaining a form or making time to listen may be useful applications. Respect the person's privacy and limits; care should not become an excuse to control their choices.
takeaway: Ask someone what practical help would make their day easier.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 2699a — Relieving distress and seeking knowledge

quiz.question: What is a good first step when offering help?
options: Assume you already know what they need
Announce their difficulty to everyone
Ask what support would be useful
quiz.explanation: Asking helps make support responsive rather than intrusive.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Make one burden lighter. Ask someone what practical help would make their day easier.

title: Humility does not need an audience
hook: Accepting a correction can be a quiet act of growth.
body: Sahih Muslim 2588 connects charity, forgiveness and humility with Allah's reward and honour. This is an explanatory paraphrase, not a promise of an immediate financial return. For a daily application, receive a fair correction without trying to win the room. Thank the person and repair what you can. Humility here is not a demand to accept abuse or abandon appropriate boundaries.
takeaway: Accept one fair correction and make one useful adjustment.

sources.title: Sahih Muslim 2588 — Charity, forgiveness and humility

quiz.question: Which response best illustrates this lesson?
options: Accepting a fair correction without a performance
Accepting abuse as a duty
Expecting instant profit after every donation
quiz.explanation: The practical reflection is humble openness, not a financial formula or surrender of safety.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Humility does not need an audience. Accept one fair correction and make one useful adjustment.

title: A suspicion is not a fact
hook: A delayed reply tells you less than your imagination might suggest.
body: Quran 49:12 warns against many suspicions, spying and backbiting. This is an explanatory paraphrase. When a message goes unanswered, separate the observation from the story: the reply has not arrived; you do not yet know why. If needed, ask respectfully. This reflection does not mean ignoring evidence of danger or avoiding appropriate support when there is a genuine concern.
takeaway: Name what you know before deciding what it means.

sources.title: Quran 49:12 — Suspicion, spying and backbiting

quiz.question: Which statement separates observation from assumption?
options: They did not reply, so they dislike me
They have not replied; I do not know why
I should search their private messages
quiz.explanation: An unanswered message is observable; the motive is not yet established.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: A suspicion is not a fact. Name what you know before deciding what it means.

title: Leave humiliation out of the joke
hook: Being funny is not the same as making someone feel small.
body: Quran 49:11 warns believers against ridicule, defamation and offensive nicknames. This is an explanatory paraphrase. In a group conversation, notice whether the joke depends on someone's appearance, background or vulnerability. You can change the subject or choose humour that does not target them. If you caused hurt, acknowledge it directly rather than insisting the other person should have found it funny.
takeaway: Choose humour that does not need a person to be the target.

sources.title: Quran 49:11 — Ridicule and offensive nicknames

quiz.question: What is the better response after a hurtful joke?
options: Repeat it until everyone laughs
Blame the person for being upset
Acknowledge the hurt and stop targeting them
quiz.explanation: Taking responsibility fits the verse's warning against ridicule and insulting labels.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Leave humiliation out of the joke. Choose humour that does not need a person to be the target.

title: Say the difficult thing better
hook: Kind wording can still be clear and firm.
body: Quran 17:53 directs Allah's servants to say what is best and warns about discord. This is an explanatory paraphrase. In disagreement, describe the specific problem instead of attacking the person's whole character. For example, explain what was missed and what needs to happen next. This practical application keeps room for honesty and boundaries without adding unnecessary insult to an already difficult conversation.
takeaway: Replace a personal attack with a specific concern and request.

sources.title: Quran 17:53 — Speaking what is best

quiz.question: Which approach best fits this lesson?
options: Describe the issue and request a clear change
Attack the person's worth
Hide every disagreement
quiz.explanation: Better wording can address a real problem clearly without insulting the person.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Say the difficult thing better. Replace a personal attack with a specific concern and request.

title: Fairness when it costs you
hook: The test of fairness is harder when your own side made the mistake.
body: Quran 4:135 calls believers to stand firmly for justice, even concerning themselves or close relatives, without letting desire distort testimony. This is an explanatory paraphrase. In an everyday disagreement, state the relevant facts even when they do not flatter your side. Admitting your part in a mistake can be a practical first step. Loyalty does not require rewriting what happened.
takeaway: Apply the same standard to your own mistake and someone else's.

sources.title: Quran 4:135 — Standing for justice

quiz.question: What is the fair response when your friend made the mistake?
options: Change the facts to protect them
Use the same factual standard you would for anyone
Assume an outsider must be at fault
quiz.explanation: The verse calls for justice even when personal relationships make it uncomfortable.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Fairness when it costs you. Apply the same standard to your own mistake and someone else's.

title: Confidence without looking down
hook: You do not need to shrink another person to stand upright.
body: Quran 31:18 warns against turning away from people in contempt and walking arrogantly. This is an explanatory paraphrase. A daily application is to greet someone whose role is often overlooked, listen without dismissing them, and avoid using status to embarrass them. Confidence and competence do not require contempt. Notice how you treat people who cannot offer you an advantage.
takeaway: Offer the same basic respect across differences in status.

sources.title: Quran 31:18 — A warning against arrogance

quiz.question: Which behaviour fits confidence without arrogance?
options: Dismissing people with less status
Using success to embarrass others
Listening respectfully regardless of someone's role
quiz.explanation: Respectful listening does not depend on another person's rank or usefulness to you.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Confidence without looking down. Offer the same basic respect across differences in status.

title: Notice one good moment
hook: Acknowledging something good does not erase what is hard.
body: The NIH Emotional Wellness Toolkit suggests noticing positive moments and practising gratitude as ways to build emotional resilience. Try recalling one helpful interaction or small comfort from today and describe it specifically. You do not need to label the whole day good. This is a general wellbeing practice, not treatment, and difficult feelings still deserve attention and support when they persist.
takeaway: Write one specific good moment without denying a hard one.

sources.title: NIH — Emotional Wellness Toolkit

quiz.question: What is the aim of noticing a good moment?
options: To acknowledge something positive without denying difficulty
To prove that distress is unreal
To replace needed professional care
quiz.explanation: A positive moment can be acknowledged alongside real difficulty; this is not a treatment claim.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Notice one good moment. Write one specific good moment without denying a hard one.

title: Make a little space around stress
hook: You may not control the whole day, but you can pause within it.
body: The NIH Emotional Wellness Toolkit recommends stress-management approaches such as relaxation, setting priorities and seeking support. Choose a small pause: sit comfortably, breathe gently without forcing it, and identify the next manageable task. This suggestion is general wellbeing advice, not a cure for anxiety. If distress persists, disrupts daily life or feels unmanageable, reach out to a qualified professional for support.
takeaway: Pause gently, then choose one manageable next step.

sources.title: NIH — Emotional Wellness Toolkit: Reduce stress

quiz.question: Which expectation is appropriate for a brief pause?
options: It guarantees that anxiety disappears
It may create space for a manageable next step
It removes the need to seek support
quiz.explanation: The practice is a modest coping suggestion, not a guaranteed cure or substitute for care.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Make a little space around stress. Pause gently, then choose one manageable next step.

title: Give sleep a regular place
hook: Rest deserves a place in the plan, not only the leftovers.
body: The NIH Emotional Wellness Toolkit identifies quality sleep as part of emotional wellbeing and suggests a consistent sleep schedule. Choose one realistic routine change, such as a steadier bedtime or a calmer wind-down. A routine is an experiment in supporting rest, not a promise that sleep problems will vanish. Persistent sleep difficulties are a reason to speak with a healthcare professional.
takeaway: Choose one realistic change that gives rest a more regular place.

sources.title: NIH — Emotional Wellness Toolkit: Get quality sleep

options: Expect perfect sleep after one night
Treat persistent problems as a personal failure
Try a consistent routine and seek help if problems persist
quiz.explanation: A routine can support sleep, while persistent difficulties may need professional assessment.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Give sleep a regular place. Choose one realistic change that gives rest a more regular place.

title: Practise returning your attention
hook: Wandering attention is a chance to return, not a reason to give up.
body: The NIH Emotional Wellness Toolkit describes mindfulness as awareness of the present moment and suggests paying attention during ordinary activities. Try noticing the feeling of your feet on the ground or the sounds around you. When attention wanders, return gently. This optional exercise is a general wellbeing suggestion. It does not require emptying your mind or promise to resolve a mental health condition.
takeaway: Notice one present sensation and gently return to it once.

sources.title: NIH — Emotional Wellness Toolkit: Be mindful

quiz.question: What can you do when attention wanders?
options: Gently return to the present activity
Decide the exercise has failed
Force every thought to disappear
quiz.explanation: Returning attention is the practical exercise; having no thoughts is not the goal.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Practise returning your attention. Notice one present sensation and gently return to it once.

title: Connection can begin with one message
hook: You do not need a perfect update to contact someone you trust.
body: The NIH Emotional Wellness Toolkit includes strengthening social connections among its wellbeing strategies. Consider a short message to someone supportive, a shared activity or asking for a listening ear. Make the invitation small and respect the other person's availability. This is general wellbeing guidance, not a replacement for professional care. If your needs are more serious, seek appropriate support rather than carrying them alone.
takeaway: Send one low-pressure invitation to connect with someone supportive.

sources.title: NIH — Emotional Wellness Toolkit: Strengthen social connections

quiz.question: Which invitation respects both people?
options: Demand an immediate reply
Ask whether they have time to talk
Treat one missed call as rejection
quiz.explanation: A low-pressure invitation leaves room for the other person's time and boundaries.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Connection can begin with one message. Send one low-pressure invitation to connect with someone supportive.

title: Close the notes and try recalling
hook: A familiar page is not the same as knowledge you can retrieve.
body: UNC's Studying 101 guide distinguishes rereading from actively working with material and recommends self-testing. After a short reading, close the page and write what you remember. Then reopen it to check accuracy and fill gaps. The attempt is useful even when incomplete because it shows what needs attention. Keep the check low-stakes and correct errors rather than rehearsing an unchecked answer.
takeaway: Recall first, then check your notes and repair the gaps.

sources.title: UNC Learning Center — Studying 101: Study Smarter Not Harder

quiz.question: What should follow an attempt to recall without notes?
options: Assume every remembered detail is right
Avoid checking mistakes
Compare with the source and correct gaps
quiz.explanation: Checking and correcting makes the recall attempt a useful learning cycle.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Close the notes and try recalling. Recall first, then check your notes and repair the gaps.

title: Return to a topic on another day
hook: A second encounter can do more than one longer sitting.
body: UNC's Studying 101 guide recommends distributing study across shorter sessions instead of relying on cramming. Choose a small topic, practise it today, and schedule another encounter on a later day. Begin the next session by trying to recall what you learned. The point is repeated engagement over time, not a perfect universal timetable. Adjust your plan to the material and your responsibilities.
takeaway: Schedule a second short session instead of leaving revision to the end.

sources.title: UNC Learning Center — Studying 101: Spaced practice

quiz.question: Which plan uses distributed study?
options: Revisiting a topic in shorter sessions across days
Saving everything for one final night
Reading once and never returning
quiz.explanation: Spacing means returning to the material over time rather than concentrating all practice at once.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Return to a topic on another day. Schedule a second short session instead of leaving revision to the end.

title: Explain it without borrowing the paragraph
hook: An explanation reveals gaps that highlighting can hide.
body: UNC's Studying 101 guide recommends active engagement, including explaining concepts in your own words and connecting ideas. Pick one concept and explain it as though helping a beginner. Add an example, then check your explanation against the source. If a step is vague, that is a useful place to investigate. Simple wording should preserve the meaning, not replace accuracy with a catchy slogan.
takeaway: Explain one idea simply, give an example, then check for accuracy.

sources.title: UNC Learning Center — Studying 101: Active engagement

options: It repeats the heading only
It preserves meaning and can be checked against the source
It avoids examples and corrections
quiz.explanation: Explaining in your own words helps when the explanation remains accurate and gaps are checked.

title: Give a study session one clear job
hook: Study more is vague; solve and check three problems is actionable.
body: UNC's Studying 101 guide recommends planning study sessions, working with focus and reducing multitasking. Before starting, choose one concrete task and put unrelated notifications aside where practical. Work on that task, then check what you accomplished. The example is a flexible study plan, not a required session length. A small finished task gives you clearer feedback than an open-ended intention to study everything.
takeaway: Write a specific finish line before beginning your next session.

sources.title: UNC Learning Center — Studying 101: Planning and focus

quiz.question: Which goal gives the clearest finish line?
options: Become good at everything
Keep several unrelated tasks open
Solve and check three practice problems
quiz.explanation: A specific task makes it possible to know what you completed and what still needs work.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Give a study session one clear job. Write a specific finish line before beginning your next session.

title: Find the gap before making the plan
hook: Your least comfortable topic may deserve more time than your favourite one.
body: UNC's Strategic Test Prep guide begins by identifying what you already know and what you do not. List the likely topics, then try recalling or solving something without looking at the notes. Use the results to decide where to focus. The check is information, not a verdict on your ability. Planning from actual gaps can keep comfortable material from consuming the whole session.
takeaway: Use a brief self-check to choose your next study priority.

sources.title: UNC Learning Center — Strategic Test Prep

quiz.question: What should guide the next study priority?
options: Gaps revealed by a self-check
Only the easiest topic
How impressive the notes look
quiz.explanation: Checking what you can retrieve helps direct effort toward material that needs more practice.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Find the gap before making the plan. Use a brief self-check to choose your next study priority.

title: Sunset is a turning-world story
hook: Your place on Earth turns out of sunlight as the planet rotates.
body: NASA explains that Earth's rotation produces the daily cycle of daylight and darkness. The side facing the Sun receives daylight, while the side turned away experiences night. A simple model is a ball beside a fixed lamp: turn the ball and watch one marked spot move between light and shadow. The demonstration models rotation; it is not a scale model of the solar system.
takeaway: Picture your location rotating between the sunlit and dark sides of Earth.

sources.title: NASA — Heliophysics Big Idea 1.1: Earth and the Sun

quiz.question: What produces the daily cycle of day and night?
options: The Moon switching sunlight off
Earth rotating
Earth stopping each evening
quiz.explanation: Rotation carries a location toward and away from the sunlit side of Earth.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Sunset is a turning-world story. Picture your location rotating between the sunlit and dark sides of Earth.

title: Night here does not mean night everywhere
hook: A dark sky above you is a local view, not the whole planet's condition.
body: NASA's explanation of the Sun-Earth system connects day and night with Earth's rotation. At any moment, one side of Earth faces the Sun while the other faces away. This helps explain why someone elsewhere can be in daylight while you are in darkness. Imagine two marked places on opposite sides of a ball beside a lamp and compare their views before rotating it.
takeaway: Separate your local sky from what another part of Earth experiences.

sources.title: NASA — Heliophysics Big Idea 1.1: Sun-Earth relationships

quiz.question: When it is night at your location, what can be true elsewhere?
options: Every location must also be dark
The Sun has stopped shining
A location facing the Sun can have daylight
quiz.explanation: Different parts of Earth face toward or away from the Sun at the same moment.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: Night here does not mean night everywhere. Separate your local sky from what another part of Earth experiences.

title: A spin and a journey are different motions
hook: Turning in place is not the same as travelling around something.
body: NASA distinguishes Earth's rotation from its orbit around the Sun. Rotation is the planet turning on its axis and is responsible for the daily light-dark cycle. Orbit is its journey around the Sun. Try turning a ball in your hand, then moving it around a lamp. Keeping those motions separate helps you ask which movement explains the observation you are trying to understand.
takeaway: Use rotation for spinning on an axis and orbit for travelling around.

options: Turning on an axis
Travelling around the Sun
Changing from liquid to vapour
quiz.explanation: Rotation is a spin on an axis; orbit describes motion around another body.

title: The Moon is not changing its shape
hook: A crescent is a view of illumination, not a piece missing from the Moon.
body: NASA explains that moonlight is reflected sunlight and that lunar phases come from our changing view of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth. The Moon itself does not become a different shape. Ordinary phases are not caused by Earth's shadow covering it; that is the explanation for a lunar eclipse. On your next observation, describe the lit portion rather than imagining a changing object.
takeaway: Distinguish the Moon's changing visible illumination from its physical shape.

sources.title: NASA — Moon Phases

quiz.question: What explains ordinary lunar phases?
options: The Moon physically changes shape
Our changing view of its sunlit half
Earth's shadow covers it every month
quiz.explanation: Phases reflect viewing geometry; Earth's shadow is involved in lunar eclipses, not ordinary phases.

media.alt: Original illustrated explanation: The Moon is not changing its shape. Distinguish the Moon's changing visible illumination from its physical shape.

title: A watery planet still needs freshwater care
hook: Seeing a planet full of water does not mean all of it is ready to drink.
body: NOAA reports that about 97 percent of Earth's water is in the ocean. That large share helps explain why total planetary water is not the same thing as freshwater available for daily use. The statistic describes where water is found, not the safety of a particular tap or stream. As a practical reflection, notice one place where you can avoid wasting treated water.
takeaway: Distinguish total water abundance from usable freshwater availability.

sources.title: NOAA — How much water is in the ocean?

quiz.question: About how much of Earth's water does NOAA place in the ocean?
options: About one quarter
About one half
About 97 percent
quiz.explanation: NOAA gives approximately 97 percent, showing why total water and accessible freshwater are different ideas.
